text:
maya: FYI, we have elevated read tail latency on eu-west2 gnode pool since ~07:08 UTC. Several GPU pods stuck in AttachVolume waiting for disk I/O.

sam: Any obvious trigger? scrub/scheduler overlap?

maya: Timeline: janitor ran a full pool scan starting 06:55. Sample iostat from host gnode-eu-12 at 07:06:

maya: ```
Device             tps    kB_read/s    kB_wrtn/s    %util
nvme0n1           410     17600         800           94.3
avg-cpu:  %user %system %iowait %idle
           1.5     4.0    20.1    74.4
```

chris: 20% iowait is bad. Did janitor obey the occupancy hints for GPU provisioning windows? We have a flag for that.

maya: Cleaner service didn't scale down. Version is janitor v2.3.7 which lacks node-occupancy gating. It used to reduce concurrency but recent rollout bumped parallel workers.

infra-bot: alert: scrub_throttle_needed eu-west2 detected 2767000018  28 hosts above iops ceiling.

lee: SMART log on one host shows rising reallocated sectors and pending reads:

lee: ```
Reallocated_Sector_Ct: 23
Current_Pending_Sector: 12

nvme smart log:  media_errors: 17, prog_fail: 3
```

sam: Pending sectors + heavy scrub => amplified retries and tail latency. We should avoid full scans during provisioning ramps.

maya: Immediate mitigation proposal:
- Pause janitor on nodes with gpu_pending > 0 for 15m
- Globally cap janitor_io_per_node to 700 IOPS
- Reduce per-scan parallelism

maya: Example config patch (to apply as ConfigMap):

maya: ```yaml
janitor:
  max_workers: 3
  iops_per_node: 700
  pause_on_gpu_pending: true
  pause_duration_minutes: 15
```

chris: Also add a quick rule: if node.nvme.pending_sectors > 0 then mark node for immediate hw-review and skip full-scan until replaced.

lee: For hosts with pending sectors > 0 we should schedule a maintenance reprovision. I'll pull a node list: kubectl get nodes -l nvme.status=pending

sre-oncall: I'll run a cluster-wide scrub throttle job now (30m), and label paused nodes with scrub=paused so janitor respects it. Want the playbook?

maya: Yes, do it. Tag nodes and start GPU scheduling resumption gradually once iowait drops.

infra-bot: action: scrub_throttle job started by sre-oncall at 2767000025  applying caps and node labels.

sam: Opening INF-4312 with mitigation steps, config diff, and rollback. Risk: delaying scrubs increases detection window for latent media errors; capture tradeoffs.

chris: Long-term: bump janitor to v2.5 with SMART-aware sampling (fast read-only probes for devices with high retry counts instead of full pool scans) and a backoff that watches kube-scheduler queue length.

lee: Also collect nvme firmware versions and nvme smart logs before any replacements: nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1 > /tmp/nvme-gnode-eu-12.log

sre-oncall: Early metrics: after throttle iowait sampled down 20% -> 5% on targeted hosts within 2 minutes. Releasing holds on lower-iowait nodes now.

maya: Good. After we stabilize, schedule targeted SMART scans during low-provision windows and plan drive replacements for hosts with persistent pending sectors. I'll update INF-4312 with a phased runbook.

sam: Runbook sketch: 1) throttle 30m, 2) label scrub-paused nodes, 3) roll ConfigMap patch, 4) cordon & reprovision worst hosts, 5) upgrade janitor to v2.5 and re-enable occupancy-aware scrubs.

lee: Noting a firmware correlation in past incidents  include firmware as a filter when choosing replacement candidates.

maya: Thanks all. I'll post metric snapshots in 10m. Marking this thread for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
